source.title: The Curious Case of Representational Alignment: Unravelling Visio-Linguistic Tasks in Emergent Communication
source.authors: Tom Kouwenhoven; Max Peeperkorn; Bram van Dijk; T. Verhoef

record.tranche_reason: The study measures alignment between emergent-communication agents and between agent representations and their image inputs. It reports that inter-agent alignment can increase while image-agent alignment declines, refining the interpretation of alignment as evidence of shared, grounded representations. It does not test convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. The paper also reports communication accuracy and TOPSIM outcomes; rows below include only results directly bearing on representational alignment or its dependence on input and measurement conditions.
record.test_reason: The study measures RSA between a speaker and listener that are jointly trained on one communication objective, and between each agent and its frozen input embeddings. These are co-adapted agents, not independently trained models of different architecture, data or scale (V1), seeds of one architecture trained separately (V3), or vision versus language models (V2). It also compares no similarity measures or settings for cross-model convergence (V6). The finding is a related but different construct and goes under fits_no_version. The ce+RSA rows add an alignment term on purpose, so they induce the behaviour. The record's V6/V7 links and limits_scope labels are not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add two points. The authors argue TOPSIM is an indirect metric of inter-agent alignment. They also say the alignment penalty prevents drift without lowering communicative success, and that agents still communicate above chance about noise.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses RSA based on pairwise cosine similarities and Spearman correlation in a referential-game setting, and adds an RSA penalty during training. It does not reproduce either original source's model-scale or cross-model convergence procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported degree of input-representation drift varies with vision module and vocabulary size; alignment trends are reported across 42 channel-capacity settings. The relationship between TOPSIM and inter-agent RSA differs between ce and ce + RSA conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the standard ce loss, RSA between jointly trained speaker and listener rises during training. Each agent's RSA to its frozen input embeddings falls. This holds across 42 channel-capacity settings and three vision encoders (drift largest for CLIP; a larger vocabulary reduces drift).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agents co-trained on a shared communication objective align their representations with each other while losing the input encoder's geometry. High alignment between models can arise from co-adaptation rather than shared grounding in the input.

fits_no_version.finding: Inter-agent RSA correlates strongly with TOPSIM under ce (r=.838). Agents trained on real images still align (RSA .428) and communicate above chance on Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In emergent communication, compositionality metrics partly track inter-agent alignment, and that alignment extends to noise inputs.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Cognitive Modeling and Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study examines a two-agent referential game rather than large, independently trained models. It does not vary model scale or separate the effects of shared data and objectives. Several alignment values are reported in plots rather than in text or tables, and no alternative similarity measures are compared.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct alignment results were left out. Communicative accuracy and other task outcomes are not alignment measurements and are omitted.

untested.parts: All: no scale sweep and no independently trained models differing in architecture, objective or data.
All: no vision-language alignment on paired data; Winoground captions are unused.
All: seeds are repeats of one jointly trained pair, not cross-seed feature comparisons.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
All: no shared interpretable features or circuits.
All: one similarity measure (RSA, cosine with Spearman), no variation in its settings, and no cross-model convergence.
All: no independently trained models, so no plateau or shared-data explanation is tested.

record.verdict_notes: Emergent-communication study of co-adapted speaker/listener agents. It neither cites nor tests the Platonic or convergent-learning claims. Its point that alignment can arise without grounding is conceptually adjacent to V7, but it concerns jointly trained models, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling or model-capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No alignment measurement between vision and language models on paired images and captions; Winoground captions are not used.

The paper uses multiple training seeds but measures alignment between jointly trained speaker and listener agents, not shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment method is tested.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
The study varies input datasets, vision modules, and communication-channel capacity, but does not compare alternative similarity measures or settings such as neighbour counts.
No scaling trend or plateau across model sizes is tested. Shared data or objectives are not experimentally separated from other causes of alignment.

reader_labels.reason: Inter-agent alignment rises, but under the standard loss both agents' alignment to input features declines; the paper also reports that drift varies by vision module and channel capacity. These results concern a small emergent-communication setup, not large independently trained models. Rows R1–R15.
